Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http //wv-av. dilg.gov.ph DILG Legal Opinion No. 05 S. 2016 (JAN 2 9 A'ITY. EUFEMIO A. SIMTIM, JR. City Legal Officer Koronadal City, South Cotabato Dear Atty. Simtim: This refers to your letter dated 04 November 2015 requesting the Department's opinion on the following: a. b. c. d. e. Is notarization part of the duties and functions of the provincial or city legal officer? If it is, does it include the duty to notarize the contracts and other documents executed by the component barangays and their officials? Ifa lawyer being considered for the position oftheprovincial or city legal ofFcer has not yet applied for or has not yet been issued a notarial commission by the Court, will it render him/her disqualified for the said position? If a lawyer is serving as a provincial or city legal officer and he/she refuses or fails to apply for notarial commission in court, will it render him/her criminally or administratively lia ble? What will be the effect if a provincial or city legal officer applies for notarial commission but the application is denied by the Court for some reason, i.e., previous violation of the rules on notarial act or non-compliance with the requirements of the rules? Would it entail any liability on his/her part? In the case of a provincial legal officer, is he/she required to notarize the documents presented to him/her by all component municipalities or cities even if his/her notarial commission is limited only within the city or municipality covered by the jurisdiction of the Court which issued his/her notarial commission? VVe also received a follow-up letter dated 25 November 2015 from Atty. Fredelyn S. Gunay, Legal Officer I V, City Legal Office, City of Koronadal, South Cotabato. As culled from the documents available, hereunder are the relevant factual antecedents: Sometime in 2005, criminal complaints for violation of Sections 3 (e) and (g) of Republic Act 3019, Malversation of Public Funds or Property and Falsification of

Public Documents falling under Articles 217, 171 and 172 of the Revised Penal Code, respectively, were filed against Mayor Fernando Miguel, then Mayor of Koronadal City, and several other city officials in connection with the purchase of Lot 8, Pls-246-D, Sheet 2, Zone III, City of Koronadal in the amount of Twenty Two Million Pesos (Php 22,000,000.00), exclusive of notarial fees, capital gains, documentary stamps, estate and transfer taxes and other related expenses, also borne by the City Government of Koronadal. The case was docketed as OMB-M-C- 04-0536-1. entitled "ARTHUR P. CONDES, ET AL. VS. FERNANDO Q. MIGUEL, ET AL" One of the issues raised therein was whether or not a legal officer, either of the province, city, or municipality, has a mandatory function to notarize documents executed by the local government units within its territorial jurisdiction. Thereafter, the Office of the Ombudsman (Mindanao) issued a Resolution dated 13 October 2005 in OMB-M-C-04-0536-L, pertinent portion of which reads: 'fxx Records show that Provincial Legal Officer Romeo S Sucaldito and Legal Officer IV [osie R. Abu Felipe, both of the Province of South Cotabato, submitted their notarial commissions in answer to this Area Office 's sub na. Apparently both lawyers can easily notarize the Deed of Sale and Extrajudicial Settlement. without any legal cost. hence saving the City of Koronadal the amount ofP419.000. (M, as paid to herein respondent Monteferio. Indeed, where a government agency is provided by law with a legal officer or office who or which can handle its legal requirements, or cases in courts, it may not be allowed to hire the service of private lawyers for a fee, chargeable against public funds. Herein, although the City of Koronadal is not complemented with a City Legal Officer, good sense merely dictates that they utilize the legal services of the Provincial Legal Office, considering they have already done so in the aforementioned (Pinto and Blanco) lawsuits. This is simply in line with COA Circular No. 98-002, hereby stating that public Tunds shall not be utilized for payment of the services ofa legal counsel or Ia w firm to represent government agencies and instrumentalities, including government owned and controlled corporations and local government units in court, or to render legal services Tor them. Granting that respondent Miguel is not prohibited from hiring the services ofa legal counsel as notary public for various deeds and contracts. and further granting that he is given legal authority to do so, prudence dictates that he exercise good counsel in a period of' acute public want and great need for austerity. He could have effortlessly solicited the legal and notarial services of' the Provincial Legal Office, therebysaving the City of Koronadal the amount of P419.OOO.OOpaid as notarial fees. but lamentably. he did not.

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, let the accompanying Information for Violation of Section 3 (c) of R.A. 3019 against City Mayor FERNANDO Q. MIGUEL, City Treasurer EUFROSINO P. INAMARGA and City Accountant IMELDA A. TAMA YO be brought to court and prosecuted. On the other hand, all charges against incumbent Vice Mayor JOSE C. LEDDA, JR., incumbent Councilors EDWIN G. ABIUS, REBECCA D BONA, SERGIO S. MORALES JR., JOSE HENRY D. AGUIRRE, ROBERTO L. SUNGA, MEL JOY B. CAMARINAS, former Councilors PABLITO S. SUBERE, GERALD PAUL C. DUREMDES, JOSE G. AGREDA, JUANITO R LAGASCA, JR., MARITES R. DOMATO, GREGORIO 13. OGOY, as well as private respondents JOSE ESTANDARTE, RUDITO ESTANDARTE, LYDIA E. CORNEJA, HENRY ESTANDARTE, TERESITA E. LICAYAN, SYLVIA E. DESUYO, ESTELITA CASTILLON, INES PLOMILLO, NANCY PLOMILLO, RONALD PLOMILLO, HELEN JENKINS, LANI ALBURO, HERNANE PLOMILLO, JR., MARIETTA MANDEOYA, REYNALDO PLOMILLO, RECHIL PLOMILLO and ATTY. JOFFREY MONTEFRIO are hereby DISMISSED. SO RESOL VED. " (Emphasis Supplied) Accordingly, on 23 May 2006, an Information was filed against Mayor Fernando B. Miguel, City Treasurer Eufrosino P. Inamarga and City Accountant Imelda A. Tamayo before the Sandiganbayan docketed as Crim Case No. SB-08-CRM-0018 entitled "People of the Philippines vs. Fernando Q. Miguel, et al." During the pendency thereof or in 2010, incumbent Koronadal City Mayor Peter B. Miguel (son of former City Mayor Fernando Q Miguel) appointed you as Legal Officer of Koronadal City, South Cotabato and authorized you to engage in private practice of law. By virtue of the said authorization, he filed a petition for notarial commission and the same was granted by the Regional Trial Court. You were re-appointed by Mayor Peter B. Miguel to the position upon the latter's re-election in 2013. When your re-appointment was considered during the session of the Sanggunian Panlungsod for concurrence, a Sangguniang Panlunsod Member asked you if the notarization of documents for the city government and its component barangays is within the scope of your duty to which you answered in the negative considering that (1) you were not yet granted a notarial commission by the Court, and (2) it is not one those duties and functions enumerated under Section 481 of the Local Government Code of 1991. Thereafter, you filed your application for renewal of notarial commission in the early part of 2015 but the RTC has not acted upon it which renders you unable to notarize any document up to the date of your letter. • On 23 February 2015, a Decision was rendered by the Sandiganbayan (2nd Division) in Crim Case No. SB-08-CRM-0018, pertinent portion of which reads:

"Having been City Mayor for many _years already prior to the purchase of the Plomillo property by the Cicy_ of Koronadal, accused Miguel knew or ought to have known that the legal services of the Provincial Legal office headed by Atty. Sucaldito can be solicited and availed of for free. rather than unnecessarily spend P419.OOO.OO in government funds to pay a private lawyer for such services. More importantly, accused Miguel knew or ought to have known that local government units are actually prohibited from engaging the services ofa private lawyer, except only in extraordinary or exceptional circumstances and under certain conditions none of which were present when he contracted the services of Atty. Montefrio. Atty. Romel S. Sucaldito. the Provincial Legal Officer of the Province of' South Cotabato. where the City of Koronadal is a component city, declared that his legal services. which include notarization of legal documents. was available and could have been availed of bv the City of Koronadal. WHEREFORE, premises considered, judgment is hereby rendered finding accused Fernando Q Miguel guilty beyond reasonable doubt of Violation of Section 3, paragraph (e) of Republic Act (R.A.) No. 3019, as amended, as charged in the Information dated May 23, 2006. Pursuant to the provisions of the Indeterminate Sentence Law, he is hereby sentenced to suffer the penalty of' imprisonment of six (6) years and one (1) month, as minimum, to eight (8) years as maximum. He shall also suffer perpetual disqualification from public office. For insufficiency of evidence, accused Eufrosino T. Inamarga and Imelda A. Tamayo are hereby acquitted. SO ORDERED. " (Emphasis Supplied) The Supreme Court issued a Resolution dated 02 September 2015 in G.R. No. 218664 (Fernando Q. Miguel vs. People of the Philippines), which states: "Considering the allegations, issues and arguments adduced in the petition for review on certiorari assailing the Decision dated 23 February 2015 and Resolution dated 25 May 2015 of the Sandiganbayan in Crim. Case No. the Court resolves to DENY the petition for failure to sufficiently show any reversible error in the assailed judgment to warrant the exercise of this Court's discretionary appellate jurisdiction. "

Thereafter, former Mayor Fernando Q. Miguel filed a Motion for Reconsideration (of the Resolution dated 2 September 2015) dated 31 October 2015 with the Supreme Court raising this as one Of the issues: The Honorable Sandiganbayan erred in finding that the Provincial Legal Officer of the Province of South Cotabato is mandatorily required to notarize the documents of the component municipalities and city of the entire province of South Cotabato. Hence, your subject request for legal opinion and being followed-up by Atty. Gunay. The Decision dated 23 February 2015 rendered by the Sandiganbayan (2nd Division) in Crim Case No. SB-08-CRM-0018, has established, albeit impliedly, that when a city has no legal officer, it behooves upon the provincial legal officer to extend legal assistance to and notarize for free the Deed of Sale executed by the city. While it is true that Decisions rendered by the Sandiganbayan are not jurisprudential and therefore cannot yet be a basis of any official actionl as it is possible that it will be eventually overturned, we cannot close our eyes to and thus brush aside the fact that the Supreme Court, the highest court of the land, already issued a Resolution dated 02 September 2015 denying the petition for review on certiorari filed by Mayor Fernando Q Miguel for failure to sufficiently show any reversible error in the Decision dated 23 February 2015 and Resolution dated 25 May 2015 of the Sandiganbayan. Accordingly, the Supreme Court affirmed all the findings of the Sandiganbayan in Crim Case No. SD-08- CRIM-0018, including that issue relative to the duty of the provincial legal officer to extend legal assistance to and notarize for free the Deed of Sale executed by the City, whenever there is no available city legal officer. In view of the foregoing and considering that the same issue is the crux of your letter-request, you are hereby advised to take utmost precaution and thus consider the development in Crim Case No. SB-08-CRM-0018 with the Supreme Court in taking future actions and/or decisions. While the parties in Crim Case No. SB-08-CRM-0018 are different from the parties involved in your instant request, the same local government unit is involved, that is, the City of Koronadal. Be that as it may, for purposes of academic discussion considering that the Department is mandated primarily to interpret the provisions of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 and without prejudice to the outcome of Crim Case No. SB-08-CRM-0018 with the Supreme Court, to which the Department must always abide, we are of the view that notarization of contracts and other documents executed by the component barangays and their officials is part of the duties and functions of the provincial or city legal officer when so provided by law or ordinance pursuant to Section 481 (b)(5) of the Local Government Code of 1991 which mandates the Provincial and City Legal Officer, and even the Municipal Legal Officer (if available), to "(E)xercise such other I It is an elementary rule under Article 8 of the New Civil Code of the Philippines that judicial decisions applying and interpreting the laws and the constitution shall form part Of our legal system.

powers and perform such other duties and functions as may be prescribed by law or ordinance. Hence, if the City of Koronadal or the Province of South Cotabato has an existing ordinance which mandates the City Legal Officer or the Provincial Legal Officer, respectively, to notarize contracts and other documents executed by the component barangays and their officials, then it becomes his duty. In the absence of such ordinance, we are of the view that it is not, due to the following reasons: 1. Section 481 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 enumerates the powers and duties of provincial, city and municipal officers, thus: Section 481. Qualifications, Terms, Powers and Duties. xxx (b) The legal ofFcer, the chief legal counsel of the local govermnent unit, shall take charge of the office of legal services and shall: (1) Formulate measures for the consideration of the Sanggunian and provide legal assistance and support to the governor or mayor, as the case may be, in carrying out the delivery of basic services and provisions of adequate facilities as provided for under Section 17 of this Code; (2) Develop plans and strategies and upon approval thereof by the governor or mayor, as the case may be, implement the same, particularly those which have to do with programs and projects related to legal services which the governor or mayor is empowered to implement and which the sanggunian is empowered to provide for under this Code; (3) In addition to the foregoing duties and functions, the legal officer shall: (i) Represent the local government unit in all civil actions and special proceedings wherein the local government unit or any official thereof, in his official capacity, is a party: Provided, That, in actions or proceedings where a component city or municipality is a party adverse to the provincial government or to another component city or municipality, a special legal officer may be employed to represent the adverse party; (ii) When required by the governor, mayor or sanggunian, draft ordinances, contracts, bonds, leases and other instruments, in volving any interest of the local government unit and provide comments and recommendations on any instrument already drawn; (iii) Render his opinion in writing on any question of law when requested to do so by the governor, mayor or sanggunian;

(iv) Investigate or cause to be investigated any local official or employee for administrative neglect or misconduct in office, and recommend appropriate action to the governor, mayor or sanggunian, as the case may be; (v) Investigate or cause to be investigated any person, firm or corporation holding any franchise or exercising any public privilege for failure to comply with any term or condition in the grant ofsuch franchise or privilege, and recommending appropriate action to the governor, mayor or sanggunian, as the case may be; (vi) When directed by the governor, mayor, or sanggunian, initiate and prosecute in the interest of the local government unit concerned any civil action on any bond, lease or other contract upon any breach or violation thereof; and (vii) Revlévv and submit recommendations on ordinances approved and execute orders issued by component units; (3) Recommend measures to the sanggunian and advise the governor or mayor as the case may be on all other matters related to upholding the rule (4) Be in the frontline of protecting human rights and prosecuting any violations thereof, particularly those which occur during and in the aftermath of man-made or natural disasters or calamities; and (5) Exercise such other powers and perform such other duties and functions as may be prescribed by law or ordinance. " While the legal officer may be required by the governor, mayor or sanggunian, to draft ordinances, contracts, bonds, leases and other instruments, involving any interest of the local government unit and provide comments and recommendations on any instrument already drawn pursuant to the aforequoted Section 481 (b)(3)(i), and extend legal assistance to the governor, mayor or sanggunian pursuant to Section 481 (b)(l) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , said provisions did not categorically include notarization of the documents so drafted by the legal officer. If it were really the intention of the framers of the Local Government Code of 1991 to make such notarization one of the duties of the legal officer, then it should have been stated in a clear and unmistakable language. The same section of the Local Government Code of 1991 enumerates the 2. qualifications for the position of legal officer, to wit: Section 481. Qualifications, Terms, Powers and Duties.

(a) No person shall be appointed legal officer unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government concerned, of good moral character, and a member of the Philippine Bar. He must have practiced his profession Tor at least five (5) years in the case of the provincial and city legal officer, and three (3) years in the case of the municipal legal officer. The term of the legal officer shall be coterminous with that of his appointing authority. The appointment of legal officer shall be mandatory Tor the provincial and city governments and optional for the municipal government. As could be gleaned from the foregoing, there was no express mention of the duty of the legal officer to notarize contracts and other documents executed by the component barangays and their officials. While practice of the legal profession was mentioned therein as one of the qualifications in order for one to be qualified as a legal officer, the Supreme Court, in the plethora of cases decided by it3, held that practice of law or practice of the legal profession encompasses any activity in or out of court, which requires the application of law, legal procedure, knowledge, training and experience. This therefore means that a lawyer is still considered practicing his profession even if he is merely representing his client's interest in court, employed in government positions requiring legal skills, etc. Practice of profession does not necessarily require that a lawyer is duly commissioned by the court to notarize. In fact, under the 2004 Rules on Notarial Practice, as amended, lawyers are not required to file a petition for notarial commission but only optional, that is, those who wish to file a petition for notarial commission. The 2004 Rules on Notarial Practice prescribe several limitations on the 3. performance of notarial acts by a lawyer duly commissioned as notary public, to wit: a. Rule III, Section 11--- A person commissioned as notary public may perform notarial acts in an lace within the territorial • ri • tion of the commissionin for a period of two (2) years commencing the first day of January of the year in which the commissioning is made, unless earlier revoked or the notary public has resigned under these Rules and the Rules of Court; and b. Rule I V, Section 2 (a)-- A nota ublic shall not reform o W act outside hi regular place of work or business; provided, however, that on certain exceptional occasions or situations, a notarial act may be performed at the request of the parties in the following sites located within his territorial jurisdiction: (1) public offices, convention halls, and similar places where oaths of office may be administered; Phil. Lawyers Association vs. Agrava, G.R. No. L-12426 (16 February 1959; Cayetano vs. Monsod, G.R. No. 100113 (03 C 991

(2) public function areas in hotels and similar places Tor the signing of instruments or documents requiring notarization; (3) hospitals and other medical institutions where a party to an instrument or document is confined for treatment; and (4) anyplace where a party to an instrument or document requiring notarization is under detention. In notarizing documents presented to him, the legal officer must consider the foregoing limitations to his notarial commission, otherwise said commission shall be revoked pursuant to Rule XI of the 2004 Rules on Notarial Practice. We hope to have guided you accordingly. V truly yours, AUS ERE A.P Undersecretary DILG • OUSI.G 2016-01- .00 02 DIR. REYNALDO M.
